source.title: Prescriptive Scaling Reveals the Evolution of Language Model Capabilities
source.authors: Hanlin Zhang; Jikai Jin; Vasilis Syrgkanis; S. Kakade

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests downstream performance predictability using observational benchmark accuracy and quantile-boundary calibration, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss or the original controlled scaling-law setup.
record.gate_note: The study measures post-trained benchmark accuracy against estimated base-model pretraining compute. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, fit the original parameter/token/compute loss laws, test compute-optimal parameter-token allocation, or test the effect of architecture shape. Its results bear on V6 only. The paper's historical descriptions of classical scaling laws and cited results are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study fits high-quantile benchmark accuracy of post-trained models as a function of log pretraining compute. It checks temporal and held-out validity, which bears directly on V6 (downstream predictability with scale). It measures no pretraining loss, allocation or architecture shape, so it bears on no other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that high-quantile post-trained accuracy is well approximated by a monotone sigmoid in log pretraining compute and is temporally stable for most tasks. Math reasoning is the exception, with a boundary that keeps advancing. They add that pretrained-model accuracy is less monotone in compute than the post-trained boundary.
record.recipe_differences: This is an observational analysis of heterogeneous post-trained language models and downstream benchmark accuracy, using high-quantile sigmoid boundaries and temporal validation. It does not use the controlled pretraining-loss measurement or compute-optimal allocation procedures of the original scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Temporal period and benchmark matter: MATH Lvl 5, and to a lesser extent IFEval, show temporal under-coverage; new MATH Lvl 5 models produce notable high-compute deviations. For the reported sigmoid fits, the authors say results are stable over reasonable smoothing and regularization settings, with degradation at λ = 10−1.

fits_no_version.finding: A size–time boundary model shows task-dependent small-model ceilings. In the late period, 13B models reach q̂0.98 ≈ 0.94 on MATH Lvl 5 but ≈ 0.52 on MMLU-Pro.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The saturation of downstream benchmarks with model size is task-dependent and shifts over time.

fits_no_version.finding: Only the first of three PCA capability factors rises monotonically with compute; PC2 and PC3 boundaries are nearly flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-driven downstream gains concentrate on a single latent capability axis.

record.problems: The central evidence is observational and reflects heterogeneous submitted models, post-training pipelines, data curation, and evaluation protocols; the authors note possible selection effects and unrepresented model families or recipes. Temporal validation is restricted to overlap in compute ranges. Many task- and split-specific diagnostics are presented in figures without values transcribed in the text, and no uncertainty intervals are reported for the main boundary results.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results exceeding the 60-row limit were left out.

untested.parts: Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss, and controlled single-recipe scaling runs. The study is observational across heterogeneous post-trained models, and compute is estimated.
Not tested; no held-out loss is measured.
Not tested; the temporal splits stay within the overlapping compute range and do not extrapolate to larger runs.
Not tested for loss exponents or the compute-optimal split.

missing.what: Adjacent-decrease (non-monotonicity) rates of pretrained accuracy versus the post-trained boundary, per task
Frontier-model boundaries: GPQA Diamond scales clearly, while MATH Lvl 5 and AIME show no gain with FLOPs. Sigmoid and I-spline losses are similar.
Open LLM Leaderboard v1: most tasks saturate by P3, with little or no gain from FLOPs except on MMLU
Bin-wise OOD coverage errors, e.g. MATH Lvl 5 down to -15.5% and IFEval -11.5% in specific bins
Post-trained MUSR boundary scales with model size although pretrained models show no clear size benefit

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is observational: heterogeneous leaderboard models with estimated compute and no uncertainty intervals. The sigmoid wins only marginally over the I-spline and binwise estimators; the key contrast is with the compute-agnostic constant. Rows r9–r14 are fitted outputs and should not carry verdict weight. Three V6 labels rest on text with no row (Fig 3c, App. H.1, App. H.2); the missing entries ask for those rows.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law loss scaling is measured.
Temporal validation predicts later post-trained benchmark accuracy from earlier observational boundaries, not loss of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller training runs.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation or compute-optimal split is estimated.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns post-trained language-model benchmark performance; it does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning scaling laws, or transfer scaling laws.

Tests observational post-trained benchmark accuracy as a function of base-model pretraining compute. It does not test downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss, nor controlled per-run scaling forecasts.

The paper compares downstream capability-boundary estimators and reports temporal shifts, but does not test whether classical pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on the setup listed in this version.

relationships.condition: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 post-trained models on BBH, GPQA, MMLU-PRO and MUSR, fit on Pt and evaluated on Pt+1; Proteus-2k held-out models on tasks other than MATH
relationships.reason: The compute-based sigmoid boundary transfers with coverage error within ±2% (r1, r2). It beats the compute-agnostic baseline (r7, r8) and upper-bounds newly evaluated models (r15).
relationships.display_finding: The sigmoid boundary transferred with coverage error within ±2%, outperformed the compute-agnostic baseline and upper-bounded newly evaluated models on the tested tasks.

relationships.condition: MATH Lvl 5, and to a lesser extent IFEval, in the earliest temporal split and in post-leaderboard releases
relationships.reason: Under-coverage and elevated pinball loss appear on the earliest split (r3–r6). The MATH boundary keeps advancing at high compute and has notable outliers (r16), so compute alone does not fix attainable accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: Early forecasts showed undercoverage and elevated pinball loss, while the MATH boundary continued advancing at high compute with notable outliers.

relationships.condition: Raw pretrained base models, versus the post-trained boundary (based on the text, Fig 3c; no row)
relationships.reason: Pretrained accuracies are often locally non-monotone in compute, with adjacent-decrease rates of about 0.27–0.36 versus about 0.05 for the post-trained boundary. Predictability holds for the post-trained envelope, not raw base-model accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: Adjacent accuracy decreases occurred at rates around 0.27–0.36 for pretrained models versus approximately 0.05 for the post-trained boundary, indicating more consistent prediction of the latter.

relationships.condition: Open LLM Leaderboard v1 tasks in period P3, except MMLU (based on the text, App. H.2; no row)
relationships.reason: The authors state that on most v1 tasks, larger FLOPs bring little or no gain in P3. They attribute this to saturation or contamination.
relationships.display_finding: During one study period, most Open LLM Leaderboard v1 tasks other than MMLU gained little or nothing from larger compute budgets, which the authors attributed to saturation or contamination.

relationships.condition: Frontier models (Epoch AI / Artificial Analysis) on MATH Lvl 5 and AIME-style math (based on the text, App. H.1; no row)
relationships.reason: The authors state these tasks show no pattern of performance gain from increasing FLOPs, while GPQA Diamond scales clearly.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing FLOPs showed no pattern of improvement on MATH Level 5 or AIME-style math, while GPQA Diamond scaled clearly.
